+# Independent adversarial audit: 61-correct-bracketing
+
+## Executive conclusion
+
+The source-only reconstruction establishes a legitimate, result-constraining
+partial-correctness theorem about the submitted translated program. The loop
+claim closes independently; the end-to-end claim closes when that separately
+proved claim is selected and trusted as its lemma; every ground example closes;
+and the full claim set closes. A fresh false result mutation builds and then
+fails at the reachable wrong Boolean. The submitted `solution.mpy` is
+byte-identical to output regenerated by the trusted translator, and the
+`solutionProgram` term used by the proof parses to exactly that constructor AST.
+
+The qualification is evidence/modeling scope, not a false theorem on the
+intended domain. The generated K semantics is a small audited model rather than
+a machine-checked refinement of CPython; it pre-binds the loop variable even
+for an empty iterable, although that local binding cannot affect this program's
+claimed return value. Also, `bracketSpec` is declared globally `[total]` while
+the negative-depth/non-opening case is uncovered. Every theorem use starts at
+nonnegative depth and preserves that condition, so the uncovered case cannot
+affect claim closure; a reviewer probe demonstrates a stuck term, not a false
+equation or false result. The ordinary-mathematical bridge from `bracketSpec`
+and the generated semantics to the prompt/canonical Python behavior is
+supported by static analysis and finite differential evidence, but it is not a
+separate machine-checked refinement theorem.
+
+## 1. Input and provenance integrity
+
+### Semantics-mode boundary
+
+The rendered mode is `GENERATED_SEMANTICS`. The trusted mount
+`/reference/reference-semantics` is absent, while the trusted reference tree
+contains exactly `canonical.py`, `prompt.py`, and `py2mpy.py`. This is the
+required mount shape; there is no infrastructure breach. See
+`evidence/01_integrity.log`.
+
+### Required artifacts and types
+
+The candidate contains regular, non-symlinked files for:
+
+- `run-input.json`, `metrics.json`, `codex-last.txt`, and
+  `codex-output.log`;
+- the structured JSONL generation trace;
+- `prompt.py`, `py2mpy.py`, `solution.py`, and `solution.mpy`;
+- `semantic.k`, `verification.k`, `spec.k`, and executable `prove.sh`.
+
+No required artifact is missing, mistyped, or symlinked, and a recursive scan
+found no candidate symlink. The candidate also contains untrusted
+`semantic-kompiled/`, `verification-kompiled/`, `__pycache__/`,
+`kore-exec.tar.gz`, and generation logs/traces. Those are additional evidence,
+not source inputs; none was copied into or used by the reconstruction.
+
+The candidate prompt and translator are byte-identical to the trusted mounts:
+
+| Artifact | SHA-256 | `cmp` |
+|---|---|---|
+| candidate and trusted `prompt.py` | `f900fc0b3f9f9e3d6380108cad345c8211f454cac5496d16402442819340e1bb` | 0 |
+| candidate and trusted `py2mpy.py` | `406485eac118431c08ef59f30f79dfa6aa9d5825408917fc5ce7c806e664db16` | 0 |
+
+`run-input.json` identifies the expected problem, bare generation condition,
+and those same hashes. `metrics.json` claims a successful, non-timeout
+generation. `codex-last.txt`, `codex-output.log`, and the trace claim successful
+concrete runs and two `#Top` proof stages. These claims were read only as
+untrusted provenance and were not credited. The exact inspection script,
+untrusted excerpts, file modes, hashes, and trace event counts are in
+`evidence/01_integrity.sh` and `evidence/01_integrity.log`.
+
+The source artifacts needed for execution were copied explicitly to
+`/tmp/audit-work/candidate-src`; the exact `cp` command exited 0 in
+`evidence/00_source_copy.log`.
+
+## 2. Program fidelity and candidate-versus-canonical checks
+
+### Natural-language and trusted-reference contract
+
+The trusted prompt restricts `brackets` to strings containing only `(` and `)`.
+Together with the examples and trusted canonical implementation, the required
+result is the standard well-bracketing predicate:
+
+1. no prefix may contain more closing than opening brackets; and
+2. the final numbers of opening and closing brackets must be equal.
+
+The trusted canonical implementation maintains a depth, rejects immediately
+after a closing bracket makes it negative, and finally checks `depth == 0`.
+The candidate maintains the same unmatched-opening count, but checks
+`count == 0` immediately before consuming a closing bracket. On the intended
+domain these branch placements are equivalent: a positive count decrements
+without becoming negative, while a zero count rejects.
+
+### Translation identity
+
+The trusted translator was run from the scratch directory:
+
+```text
+python3 /reference/py2mpy.py solution.py > regenerated-solution.mpy
+```
+
+It exited 0 (`evidence/02_regenerate_mpy.log`). `cmp -l
+regenerated-solution.mpy solution.mpy` also exited 0 with no output
+(`evidence/03_mpy_byte_identity.log`). Thus the submitted `solution.mpy` is the
+trusted translation of the submitted `solution.py`, byte for byte.
+
+### Independent Python differential test
+
+`evidence/02_differential.py` independently imports
+`/reference/canonical.py:correct_bracketing` and the scratch copy of the
+candidate entry point. It covers:
+
+- all four documented examples;
+- empty input, single-character inputs, both two-character orders, unmatched
+  final openings, bad closing prefixes, nested and adjacent balanced strings,
+  and long boundary patterns;
+- every string over `{(,)}` through length 12;
+- deterministic random strings of lengths 0 through 256 with seed `610061`.
+
+After de-duplication, 10,091 inputs were compared, with 203 true and 9,888
+false results and zero mismatches. The script, exact command, selected inputs,
+exit 0, and results are preserved in `evidence/02_differential.py` and
+`evidence/04_python_differential.log`.
+
+This finite run is strong empirical evidence and exercises every candidate
+branch boundary. It is not substituted for the K proof or claimed as a
+universal equivalence proof.
+
+## 3. Clean proof reconstruction
+
+### Fresh builds
+
+The audit used K v7.1.293 and Python 3.10.12. Candidate-provided kompiled
+definitions and caches were not copied or referenced.
+
+From `/tmp/audit-work/candidate-src`, the generated semantics was freshly built
+with:
+
+```text
+timeout 300s kompile semantic.k --main-module MPY \
+  --syntax-module MPY-SYNTAX --backend llvm \
+  --output-definition semantic-audit-kompiled
+```
+
+It exited 0 (`evidence/05_kompile_semantics.log`). The proof definition was
+freshly built with:
+
+```text
+timeout 300s kompile verification.k --main-module MPY-VERIFICATION \
+  --syntax-module MPY-SYNTAX --backend haskell \
+  --output-definition verification-audit-kompiled
+```
+
+It exited 0 (`evidence/07_kompile_verification.log`).
+
+### Concrete reconstruction of generated semantics
+
+`evidence/03_semantics_differential.py` embeds the actual submitted
+`solution.mpy` in `Run(...)`, executes the fresh LLVM definition, and compares
+the final `boolVal` with both Python implementations. Fourteen cases cover an
+empty loop, an opening increment, a zero-depth early close, a positive-depth
+decrement, true/false final depth, nested/adjacent pairs, bad prefixes, and a
+32-character balanced case. Every `krun` exited 0 and all three results agreed;
+there were zero mismatches. Full final configurations, including maps, are in
+`evidence/06_semantics_differential.log`.
+
+### Positive proof claims
+
+Each positive claim was addressed against the fresh Haskell definition:
+
+| Target | Exact selection | Exit/output | Evidence |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| loop invariant | `kprove spec.k --definition verification-audit-kompiled --spec-module SPEC -I . --claims SPEC.loop` | 0, `#Top` | `evidence/08_kprove_loop.log` |
+| main, using the separately proved lemma | `kprove spec.k --definition verification-audit-kompiled --spec-module SPEC -I . --claims SPEC.loop,SPEC.main --trusted SPEC.loop` | 0, `#Top` | `evidence/15_kprove_main_with_selected_lemma.log` |
+| example `(` | `--claims SPEC.example-open --trusted SPEC.loop` | 0, `#Top` | `evidence/10_kprove_example_open.log` |
+| example `()` | `--claims SPEC.example-pair --trusted SPEC.loop` | 0, `#Top` | `evidence/11_kprove_example_pair.log` |
+| example `(()())` | `--claims SPEC.example-nested --trusted SPEC.loop` | 0, `#Top` | `evidence/12_kprove_example_nested.log` |
+| example `)(()` | `--claims SPEC.example-bad-prefix --trusted SPEC.loop` | 0, `#Top` | `evidence/13_kprove_example_bad_prefix.log` |
+| complete specification | no `--claims`, with `--trusted SPEC.loop` | 0, `#Top` | `evidence/26_kprove_all_claims.log` |
+
+The main claim alone was also attempted twice with `SPEC.loop` named only in
+`--trusted` but omitted from the selected claim set. Those attempts emitted no
+proof result before reviewer bounds of 600 and 1,200 seconds and exited 124
+(`evidence/09_kprove_main.log`, `evidence/14_kprove_main_retry.log`). This
+alternative selection is not credited as success or treated as candidate
+failure. The resolved proof route selects the already independently proved
+lemma alongside `SPEC.main`; that route and the complete-specification route
+both terminate with exit 0 and literal `#Top`.
+
+## 4. Adequacy and real-program pinning
+
+### Plain-language claim contracts
+
+| Claim | Precondition | Postcondition |
+|---|---|---|
+| `SPEC.loop` | The computation is at the exact real loop head, followed by the exact final return; `count=N`, `N >= 0`; the environment contains exactly `bracket`, `brackets`, and `count`; functions are arbitrary and unchanged. | Execution reaches exactly `boolVal(bracketSpec(N,S))`; final local environment may be any map. |
+| `SPEC.main` | Empty function and environment maps; execute `Run(solutionProgram,"correct_bracketing",S)` for an arbitrary K String `S`. | Reach exactly `boolVal(bracketSpec(0,S))`; final maps are existentially constrained, not assumed. |
+| Four examples | Same realizable empty initial maps and exact `Run(solutionProgram,...)`, with each documented ground input. | Reach the documented ground Boolean. |
+
+These are equality-style reachability destinations, not tautologies, free
+result variables, or one-way implications. The returned Boolean is fixed by
+`bracketSpec`, and the four examples fix it to a Boolean constant.
+
+### Actual program identity
+
+The main and example `<k>` cells execute `Run(solutionProgram,...)`.
+`solutionProgram` has one definitional equation whose right-hand side is the
+translated module. The translator's external syntax represents the empty
+`else` statement list by omission, while K rule syntax spells the same list
+unit `.Stmts`; therefore raw whitespace-stripped text differs. The independent
+pinning script parsed both with the fresh K definition and compared KAST terms:
+they are equal. It also confirmed the main claim contains the required
+`Run(solutionProgram,...)`. See `evidence/06_pinning_check.py` and
+`evidence/20_program_pinning.log`.
+
+The loop claim body is the exact `For` body from that term, with the exact
+trailing final `Return`. It contains no arbitrary continuation suffix. Its
+environment matches the real state reached after invocation, `count = 0`, and
+loop initialization. Thus the trusted use of the separately proved loop claim
+is confined to its proved control context rather than bypassing a different
+program region.
+
+### Satisfying states and ground substitution
+
+Every precondition is satisfiable:
+
+- main/examples: the configuration's declared initial `.Map` function and
+  environment cells, with the respective `Run` term;
+- loop: for example `N=0`, `S=""`, `CURRENT=""`, `ORIGINAL=""`,
+  functions `.Map`, and the exact three-entry environment; also
+  `N=2`, `S="))"` is a nontrivial satisfying loop state.
+
+`evidence/05_claim_witnesses.py` substitutes main inputs `""`, `"(()())"`,
+and `")"` and loop inputs `(N,S)=(0,""),(2,"))"),(1,"))")`. For loop states,
+`"(" * N + S` supplies a corresponding full entry input. The claimed summary,
+trusted canonical Python, and submitted Python agree in every case; see
+`evidence/17_claim_witnesses.log`.
+
+## 5. Rule-by-rule static soundness review
+
+### Complete local declaration inventory
+
+`semantic.k` declares:
+
+- `Pgm`: `Module(Stmts)` and the audit/execution wrapper
+  `Run(Pgm,String,String)`;
+- the empty-separator `Stmts` list and one-string `Params`;
+- `Stmt`: `FuncDef`, `Assign`, `For`, `If`, and `Return`;
+- `Expr`: `Name`, `Int`, `Bool`, `Str`, `BinOp`, and `Compare`;
+- `CmpOp`;
+- runtime `Value`: integer, Boolean, and string values;
+- the `Value` injection into `Expr`, stored `Function`, and ten control
+  `KItem` constructors (`invoke`, assignment/if/binop/compare/for
+  continuations, and `returnNow`);
+- one configuration with `<k>`, `<functions>`, and `<env>` cells.
+
+`verification.k` adds exactly two function declarations:
+`solutionProgram : Pgm [function,total]` and
+`bracketSpec : Int × String -> Bool [function,total]`.
+
+There are no local `functional` declarations, opaque symbols, priority rules,
+macros, anywhere rules, or ordinary proof-bypass rules. The only local
+`simplification` attributes are on the four `bracketSpec` equations. There are
+no additional helper K source files. The mechanically generated inventory,
+counts (32 semantic rules, 5 verification rules, 6 claims), numbered source,
+and hashes are in `evidence/04_rule_inventory.sh` and
+`evidence/16_rule_inventory.log`.
+
+### Used-syntax coverage
+
+Every constructor in `solution.mpy` is covered:
+
+| Used constructor | Declaration and behavior |
+|---|---|
+| `Module`, statement concatenation, empty statements | S2-S4 below |
+| `FuncDef`, `Params` | S5-S6 |
+| `Assign`, `Name` | S10, S19-S21 |
+| `For` | S27-S32 |
+| `If` | S22-S24 |
+| `Return` | S25-S26 |
+| `Int`, `Bool`, `Str` | S7-S9 |
+| `BinOp("+",...)`, `BinOp("-",...)` | S11-S14 |
+| `Compare(...,CmpOp("==",...))` | S15-S18 |
+
+No used constructor is parsed but left without execution rules.
+
+### All 32 semantic rules
+
+| ID | Rule role | Decision |
+|---|---|---|
+| S1 (`semantic.k:65`) | `Run(Module(...),F,input)` loads the module then invokes `F` with a string value. | Correct for the one-argument target entry call. |
+| S2 (`:67`) | Unwrap `Module` to its statements. | Correct. |
+| S3 (`:68`) | Empty statement list becomes empty computation. | Correct list base case. |
+| S4 (`:69`) | Execute the first statement before the remaining list. | Correct sequential order. |
+| S5 (`:71-72`) | Store a function definition in the function map. | Correct for the target; replacement also matches Python's last binding behavior. |
+| S6 (`:74-76`) | Look up the named function, execute its body, and create a parameter-only local environment. | Correct for this single top-level call; no caller frame is needed by the target. |
+| S7 (`:79`) | Integer literal to integer value. | Correct. |
+| S8 (`:80`) | Boolean literal to Boolean value. | Correct. |
+| S9 (`:81`) | String literal to string value. | Correct. |
+| S10 (`:82-83`) | Variable lookup in the environment. | Correct; absent names visibly stick rather than fabricate a value. |
+| S11 (`:85`) | Start `BinOp` by evaluating the left operand. | Correct left-to-right order. |
+| S12 (`:86`) | Save the left value, then evaluate the right operand. | Correct. |
+| S13 (`:87`) | Integer `+`. | Correct arbitrary-precision integer addition. |
+| S14 (`:88`) | Integer `-`. | Correct operand orientation: saved left minus evaluated right. |
+| S15 (`:90`) | Start comparison by evaluating its left operand. | Correct. |
+| S16 (`:91-92`) | Save the left value, then evaluate the comparison right operand. | Correct. |
+| S17 (`:93-94`) | Integer equality. | Correct. |
+| S18 (`:95-96`) | String equality. | Correct. |
+| S19 (`:99`) | Evaluate assignment RHS before updating the named LHS. | Correct for the target's `Name` lvalues. |
+| S20 (`:100-101`) | Replace an existing environment binding. | Correct. |
+| S21 (`:102-104`) | Add an absent binding under a negative membership guard. | Correct; the guard is disjoint from S20. |
+| S22 (`:106`) | Evaluate the `If` guard before selecting a branch. | Correct. |
+| S23 (`:107`) | Select the true branch. | Correct. |
+| S24 (`:108`) | Select the false branch. | Correct and disjoint from S23. |
+| S25 (`:110`) | Evaluate a return expression before returning. | Correct. |
+| S26 (`:111`) | Replace `value ~> returnNow ~> rest` by the value, discarding the remaining function computation. | Correct early-return control for this top-level, no-call-stack target. It discards the loop/final-return suffix exactly when Python returns. |
+| S27 (`:115`) | Evaluate the `For` iterable before loop setup. | Correct. |
+| S28 (`:116-117`) | For an existing loop-variable binding, initialize it to `""` and create `forLoop`. | The pre-initialization is harmless for the target because every nonempty iteration overwrites it before the body. See modeling caveat below. |
+| S29 (`:118-120`) | Add an absent loop-variable binding as `""`, guarded by non-membership. | Disjoint from S28 and harmless to the claimed return; caveat below. |
+| S30 (`:121`) | Empty remaining string terminates the loop. | Correct zero-iteration/base behavior. |
+| S31 (`:122-127`) | For nonempty string and existing loop variable, bind the first character, execute the body, then recurse on the tail. | Correct target iteration order and state update; string length strictly decreases. |
+| S32 (`:128-135`) | Same nonempty step when the loop binding is absent, adding it under a negative membership guard. | Correct and disjoint from S31; the real target normally reaches S31 after S29. |
+
+Evaluation is deterministic on the target: the existing/absent map rules have
+complementary guards, Boolean branches are disjoint, value-sort equality rules
+are disjoint, and empty/nonempty loop rules are disjoint. There are no local
+priorities or overlapping right-hand sides needing priority justification.
+The only allocated state is the function map and local environment map; the
+program uses no heap, I/O, exception, object allocation, or nested call.
+
+The deliberate S28/S29 pre-binding differs from CPython on empty input:
+CPython's loop target remains unbound if no iteration occurs, while the K final
+local map contains `bracket |-> strVal("")` (visible in
+`evidence/06_semantics_differential.log`). The model already abstracts away
+Python frame destruction, and every theorem makes the final environment
+existential. The target never reads `bracket` after the loop, so this
+difference cannot influence control or return value. It is an adequacy
+limitation, not an execution oracle or a witness to a false claimed result.
+
+### All 5 verification rules and proof-extension classification
+
+| ID | Extension and class | Decision |
+|---|---|---|
+| V1 (`verification.k:10-24`) | `solutionProgram`; definitional ground summary. | Its sole equation parses to the exact submitted constructor AST. It does not replace program execution; `Run`, module loading, invocation, body, loop, and return all execute under S1-S32. Its `[total]` declaration is covered by the one ground constant. |
+| V2 (`:32`) | Empty-string `bracketSpec`; mathematical simplification. | Correct: accept exactly when current unmatched depth is zero. |
+| V3 (`:33-36`) | Nonempty leading `(`; mathematical simplification. | Correct; increments depth and recurses on a strictly shorter string. |
+| V4 (`:37-39`) | Nonempty non-`(` at depth zero; mathematical simplification. | Correctly returns false, matching the program's early return. On the prompt domain this is exactly the unmatched-`)` case. |
+| V5 (`:40-44`) | Nonempty non-`(` at positive depth; mathematical simplification. | Correctly decrements depth and recurses on a strictly shorter string. |
+
+V2-V5 have disjoint guards on the theorem domain `N >= 0` and cover it
+exhaustively. Their right-hand sides agree with ordinary integer/string
+mathematics and the source control flow. They neither encode an unconnected
+oracle nor introduce a fresh result: `bracketSpec` is fully determined on every
+reachable use.
+
+The declaration `bracketSpec [total]` is nevertheless broader than its
+equations. For `N < 0`, a nonempty string not starting with `(` matches none of
+V2-V5. The reviewer claim `bracketSpec(-1,")") => false` builds and then exits
+1 with a residual unreduced `bracketSpec(-1,")")`
+(`evidence/spec-totality-probe.k`,
+`evidence/24_totality_probe_dry_run.log`,
+`evidence/25_totality_probe.log`). This is a concrete totality-coverage gap.
+It is not evidence that a false equation is enabled: the term stays stuck.
+Every entry use starts at zero, and `SPEC.loop` requires nonnegative `N`; V3-V5
+preserve nonnegativity or return false. Therefore the gap is unreachable in
+the claims and on the intended input domain. Consistent with the required
+decision rule, this review records the narrower gap rather than labeling a
+rule unsound without a false-conclusion witness.
+
+### Loop lemma as an operational summary
+
+When trusted in the main proof, `SPEC.loop` accelerates execution and is
+therefore treated as an operational summary. Its connection theorem is the
+independent successful proof in `evidence/08_kprove_loop.log`.
+
+- Matched context: exact loop body, exact remaining string, exact trailing
+  final return, exact three-binding environment, arbitrary unchanged function
+  map, and `N >= 0`.
+- Justification scope: the independently proved claim has the identical
+  configuration and guard.
+- Context containment: there is no `...` or arbitrary continuation after the
+  trailing return in the claim's `<k>` cell.
+- State footprint: functions are unchanged; loop locals execute normally; the
+  final local environment is existential because the theorem concerns the
+  return value.
+- Value origin: `bracketSpec` is fixed by V2-V5; it is not opaque or fresh.
+
+A separate reviewer body-sensitivity mutation changes only initial
+`count = 0` to `count = 1`. Its Haskell definition and spec both build, and the
+empty-input proof then fails at the reached `boolVal(false)` instead of the
+original `boolVal(true)`. See `evidence/verification-body-mutant.k`,
+`evidence/spec-body-sensitivity.k`, and
+`evidence/21_kompile_body_mutant.log` through
+`evidence/23_body_mutant_proof.log`. Thus the theorem is sensitive to the
+program-defined body.
+
+### Static soundness conclusion
+
+No local rule, simplification, totalization use, trusted claim, or opaque
+symbol was found that can enable a false return-value conclusion on the
+intended input domain. Accordingly, this report makes no unsupported
+“unsound rule” allegation. The totality and empty-loop-local issues above are
+explicitly narrower, witnessed limitations.
+
+## 6. Fresh non-vacuity test
+
+There was no candidate `spec-vacuity.k` to credit. The reviewer created
+`evidence/spec-vacuity.k`, which keeps the realizable empty initial maps and
+actual `Run(solutionProgram,...)` computation but changes the required empty
+input result from true to false.
+
+The mutation first built successfully:
+
+```text
+kprove spec-vacuity.k --definition verification-audit-kompiled \
+  --spec-module SPEC-VACUITY -I . --dry-run
+```
+
+Exit: 0 (`evidence/18_vacuity_build.log`).
+
+The real mutation proof:
+
+```text
+kprove spec-vacuity.k --definition verification-audit-kompiled \
+  --spec-module SPEC-VACUITY -I .
+```
+
+exited 1 with `WarnStuckClaimState`. The residual final configuration contains
+`boolVal(true)` and cannot unify with the destination `boolVal(false)`;
+there is no parser, import, timeout, or unrelated crash. The empty input
+satisfies the precondition and both Python implementations return true.
+The exact command and complete bounded residual are in
+`evidence/19_vacuity_proof.log`. This is valid non-vacuity evidence.
+
+## 7. Proven versus assumed accounting
+
+### What the reachability proof establishes
+
+Under the submitted K definition, for every K String `S`, executing the exact
+submitted constructor program from empty function/environment maps reaches:
+
+```text
+boolVal(bracketSpec(0,S))
+```
+
+The proof also independently establishes the nonnegative-depth loop summary
+and the four documented ground examples. As required, this is reported as
+partial correctness; neither generation prose nor finite testing substitutes
+for the K reachability proof.
+
+On strings over `{(,)}`, V2-V5 are the usual unmatched-opening recurrence:
+empty succeeds at depth zero, `(` increments, `)` at zero fails, and `)` at
+positive depth decrements. An induction on string length connects that
+recurrence to prefix nonnegativity plus final zero. The candidate and canonical
+loops maintain the same quantity; their only difference is whether the
+zero-depth check occurs immediately before or after decrementing on `)`.
+
+### Trust and limitation ledger
+
+| Boundary | Dependents | Status |
